title: Nevada lithium construction, water, qualification, and operating evidence
local_system: Nevada Lithium And Battery Materials Corridor
question: When do Nevada's authorized and financed lithium projects become built, compliant, qualified, and sustained material supply?
why_it_matters: Resource estimates, permits, and federal credit are meaningful but do not establish deliverable battery material, environmental performance, customer acceptance, or scale.
current_support: The dossier now links Thacker Pass federal and state authorizations, its closed DOE loan, Rhyolite Ridge federal and DOE environmental decisions, Nevada water-rights administration, and national mineral rails.
missing_evidence: project-specific water rights, pumping, monitoring, and impacts
inspection, compliance, mitigation, and enforcement outcomes
qualified product, customer acceptance, shipments, and sustained output
operating cost, recovery, loan performance, and local outcomes
likely_source_types: DOE loan disbursement and project update
candidate_records: Thacker Pass construction and commissioning milestones
Thacker Pass water-right, pumping, and monitoring records
Rhyolite Ridge final loan or financial-close record
first qualified production and shipment records
next_action: Follow each named project from its current authorization or finance stage into water, construction, compliance, commissioning, qualification, production, and local outcomes.

named_records: BLM Thacker Pass Record of Decision
Nevada DEP Thacker Pass permit stack
BLM and DOE Rhyolite Ridge decisions
latest_review.stage_result: The two project trails now separate federal authorization, state permits, financial close, and environmental clearance. Construction, compliance, qualification, operation, and scale remain open.
latest_review.stop_rule: Do not convert a resource estimate, authorization, permit, projected capacity, or loan decision into built, compliant, qualified, or operating supply.

notes: Phase 55U uses two named projects to make the corridor's conversion stages comparable.
